target_customer: Software teams that want automated QA and UX testing, especially those shipping fast with AI-assisted coding
problem: Manual testing is slow and misses bugs, UX flaws and broken flows before real users hit them. Swarms of AI synthetic users mimic user behavior to test end to end.
business_model: B2B SaaS for automated testing; pricing not found
product_category: AI-driven software QA and UX testing

founders.name: Aaron Chew
founders.background_notes: YC page: USACO finalist, first hire at fun.xyz, Z-Fellow.

founders.name: Kavan Doctor
founders.background_notes: YC page: ranked number 1 in math in Canada.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that drive real UIs and judge UX quality build on foundation models and browser automation; reliability across apps is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: AI testing agents were being built by many teams and rely on the same underlying models, so copying is quick.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against the company found.

market_need_then: AI-assisted coding was increasing release speed in 2025, so testing became a bottleneck, per the company's own pitch on its YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; searches returned Synthesia and Artificial Societies, which are different companies with similar names.

pivots.from: Synthetic videos to power marketing (YC directory tagline)
pivots.to: Synthetic users for automated QA and UX testing
pivots.why: Not stated; the directory tagline conflicts with the YC page and company site, and sources do not explain why.

Its tagline suggests it may have changed direction from marketing video to QA, but sources do not explain the change, so no factors are assigned.
